newsitem.title: UK: Mark crosses keep to narrow ranges in quiet Europe.
newsitem.headline: Mark crosses keep to narrow ranges in quiet Europe.

text.p: The mark was steady on its European crosses in morning Europe, barely changed from Monday's levels and taking little notice of today's soft inflation data out of Germany, France and Italy.

Mark/lira eased off earlier levels but remained within recent ranges just above 990 lire. Italian March PPI rose 0.9 percent year-on-year against a previous 0.8 rise, but analysts said a near-term Italian rate cut is likely to be put off until details emerge of the government's three-year economic plan.

"The fiscal side is so negative for the time being, the Bank of Italy has probably decided it's better to wait to see what's in the three-year programme before cutting rates," said Ernesto Ramirez, European economist at Bankers Trust in London.
The three-year plan, which contains the government's economic targets for 1998-2000, is expected at the end of May to early June.

Despite the EU Commission's report Monday that Italy's spending controls were insufficient and more sustainable measures would be needed for monetary union participation, the lira and Italy's bond markets remained fairly sanguine.
Mark/lira was trading at 990.40/90 at 0920 GMT against 991.65/80 in late Europe on Monday.
Pan-German April CPI was unchanged month-on-month and posted a gain of just 1.4 percent for the year, in line with an average of analysts' forecasts.
The data had little impact, though dealers said they did reinforce the outlook of steady German rates for the time being.
France also posted soft inflation data, with April CPI flat to 0.1 percent higher and up 0.9-1.0 percent year-on-year, the lowest for 40 years, said analysts.

"This is well below the Bank of France's 2.0 percent CPI target but the key issue for politicians is whether the voters see this as a cause for celebration or as a reflection of the depressed state of the French economy over the past few years," said Nick Parsons, forex strategist at Paribas.
Mark/French franc stood at 3.3709/14 against 3.3707/12 late Monday.
But the market's focus remains on the forthcoming French elections as the centre-right ruling coalition continues to lead in the latest opinion polls.

However, analysts said the outcome was far from decided. Extreme-right National Front leader Jean-Marie Le Pen said today he would prefer the left to win the election, mainly as an obstruction to President Jacques Chirac's EMU-driven austerity measures.

Le Pen's party holds 13.5-16 percent of the vote according to opinion polls, but the concern is how those votes will be transferred where the National Front candidate is eliminated in the first round.
"We will have to see how the (first round) breakdown comes out. It could split the vote of the right," said Bankers Trust's Ramirez.

The Norwegian crown pulled off its five-month lows against the mark, bolstered slightly by today's revised budget for this year. Norway upgraded its 1997 overall GDP growth forecast to 3.9 percent from 3.1 and left unchanged the CPI forecast at 2.5 percent.

Meantime, Norway's finance ministry said it may invest 30 to 50 percent of the State Petroleum Fund into overseas stock exchanges. The ministry said the fund may grow to 425 billion crowns by the end of 2001 from today's 50 billion crowns.
The crown stood at 4.1600/30 per mark at 1018 GMT after touching a 4.1870 low in earlier trade. It traded at 4.1670/1700 in Europe late on Monday.
